dedupe_keys.name: gsa gambod mobile industry databases devices networks spectrum chipsets

description: GAMBoD is a set of six databases on 3GPP mobile technologies maintained by the Global mobile Suppliers Association. Contents and size: Devices (about 30,000 devices, 112 attributes), Public Networks (about 4,000 networks, 44 attributes), Private Networks (1,500 customers, 89 attributes), Operators (about 1,400 operators, 44 attributes), Chipsets (about 400 chipsets, 128 attributes) and Spectrum Assignment (about 9,000 assignments, 9 attributes). The page says results can be filtered by device type, technology feature set and spectrum, searched by region or country, and displayed as tables and graphs that can be exported into reports if GSA is referenced as the source; 2G and 3G sunsetting is tracked. Producer: GSA, whose research team updates the databases monthly or quarterly. Coverage: global. Access: launched from the GAMBoD page; the page tells members having trouble to log out and back in, and offers free user registration for GSA reports, so registration is recorded as required and the free scope should be checked. Licence and cost: export for reports with attribution; the exact free versus member split was not confirmed, hence freemium. Caveats: a commercial-industry database, network fields depend on operator disclosure and no bulk download is described. Simulation uses: it supplies spectrum and technology deployment per operator for capacity-planning and technology-sunset scenarios. Related record: ITU ICT statistics (data-itu-ict-statistics).
